relevance_note: Cohort paper whose Table 2 attributes specific homozygous LPIN2 variants to single Majeed syndrome patients (rows with n = 1, 1 and 2): 'Majeed syndrome (LPIN2 mutation) was diagnosed in four patients'.
method_note: Single-centre cohort of 200 SAID patients (38 rare monogenic). Four Majeed syndrome patients are in scope; the paper gives no patient labels, so labels follow Table 2 data rows (LPIN2 rows are data rows 6, 7 and 8). Table 2 row 8 (c.838 C>T p.Arg280Ter, n = 2) covers two people; they are labelled 'Table 2 row 8' and 'Table 2 row 8 2' (suffix convention borrowed from label rule 4) and cannot be told apart. Zygosity (Homozygous) comes from each person's own Table 2 row; the 'AR' Inheritance column is mode of inheritance, not variant origin, so inheritance is 'not reported'. Table 1 Majeed row is group-level only (median onset 5 months, F (3), First degree CM2 (50), Recurrent fever (2), Skin rash (3), Vomiting/diarrhea (2), Amyloidosis (1), CKN (1)); these counts were not assigned to anyone. Features were assigned to all four from the named-group text statement ('four patients, all of whom exhibited ...') and from Table 1 counts equal to the group size (Bone lesions (4), Elevated APR (4), CS (4), ANK (4)), recorded as 'inferred from group statement'. APR is not defined in the Table 1 legend; the paper elsewhere writes 'acute-phase reactants'. Contradictions: (1) text says none of the four Majeed patients had cutaneous manifestations (Results and Discussion), but Table 1 lists 'Skin rash (3)' for the Majeed row; the excluded rows are emitted and the narrower checklist item 'neutrophilic dermatosis (Sweet syndrome)' is left not reported. (2) Consanguinity: Results say 'all patients had positive consanguineous marriage' for the 38 rare SAID patients, but Table 1 gives 'First degree CM2 (50)' for Majeed and the Discussion says 78%; consanguinity left not reported. (3) Table 1 prints p.R562X while Table 2 prints p.Arg562Ter (same notation difference, not a conflict). Bone inflammation / bone lesions not mapped to the CRMO checklist item because the paper does not name CRMO. Spans were cut from the paper text by script (the HGVS cells contain no-break and thin spaces) and all were verified verbatim.
